parts.question: Compare AE evidence in HN-204 and HN-311.

result.answer:
In HN-204, the treatment-emergent adverse events for AX-17 and Control groups were: Nausea 12.7% and 6.0% respectively, Headache 14.0% and 6.6%, Fatigue 15.3% and 7.2%, Dizziness 16.6% and 7.8%, Rash 17.8% and 8.4%, and Transaminase elevation 19.1% and 9.0% [E1, E3]. Transaminase elevation was serious, while Nausea, Headache, Fatigue, Dizziness, and Rash were not serious [E1]. The highest treatment % in HN-204 was transaminase elevation (19.1%) [E4].

In HN-311, the treatment-emergent adverse events for AX-17 and Control groups were: Nausea 11.8% and 6.0% respectively, Headache 13.0% and 6.6%, Fatigue 14.2% and 7.2%, Dizziness 15.4% and 7.8%, Rash 16.6% and 8.4%, and Transaminase elevation 17.7% and 9.0% [E2, E3]. Transaminase elevation was serious, while Nausea, Headache, Fatigue, Dizziness, and Rash were not serious [E2]. The highest treatment % in HN-311 was transaminase elevation (17.7%) [E4].

Comparing HN-311 to HN-204, the treatment % differences (HN-311 minus HN-204) were: Nausea -0.9 points, Headache -1.0 points, Fatigue -1.1 points, Dizziness -1.2 points, Rash -1.2 points, and Transaminase elevation -1.4 points [E4]. All treatment % differences (HN-311 minus HN-204) lie between -1.4 and -0.9 points [E4]. For all listed adverse events, the control % difference (HN-311 minus HN-204) was +0.0 points [E4].
